citation.title: Temporal super-resolution of kinetic plasma profiles at COMPASS using neural networks
citation.authors: Imrisek M, Seidl J, Odložilík M, Šos M, Bílková P, Böhm P, Aksoy H, Scapini Weiand R, Alcaraz Aguado I, Mahieu R, Naydenkova D
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1088/1361-6587/ae72c6 (this paper's own DOI, PDF p.2 header)

scope_read.limitations: PDF page = printed page + 1. Figure values were read visually. The proposed key misspells the surname; the paper uses Imrisek (Imríšek in ref [25]).

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Past slow measurements are not used as inputs; fast signals map to TS-target profiles
claim_checks.source_finding: Inputs are AXUV, SXR, interferometer, Dα/CIII, IPR, Ip, Uloop, coil supplies and position. TS profiles serve only as training targets. The MLP maps a single input snapshot to a profile.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p.3 Sec.1 (para 2); p.4-5 Sec.2.1, Table 1; p.8 Fig.5
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: On COMPASS, a fully connected network mapped fast radiation, magnetic, interferometric and spectroscopic signals to Thomson-scattering Te and ne profiles, with Thomson data used only as training targets.
claim_checks.qualification: No past-target anchors and no temporal history are used. Causality is not discussed.

claim_checks.source_finding: For the radiation-only model, Te error SD is about 10% in the core and about 20% at the edge; ne is broader. Radiation-only MAPE: Te about 5/16/32% (core/edge/near-SOL), ne about 12/15/24%. Table 3 gives lower values, e.g. Te edge 10.9% with smoothed inputs; that table's input set is not stated.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p.8-9 Sec.3.1, Fig.7; p.10 Fig.8; p.11-12 Fig.12; p.14 Table 3
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Reported edge errors were of order 10-20%, rising in the scrape-off layer, relative to Thomson labels.
claim_checks.qualification: Errors are measured against TS labels only, at TS times. Metrics differ between figures.

claim_checks.source_finding: An 80/20 split by discharge, plus five-fold cross-validation on the training set. Data cover shots 17000-21812.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Validation used held-out discharges with k-fold cross-validation.
claim_checks.qualification: Chronological ordering and a separate untouched test set are not stated.

input_target_timing.inputs: Fast signals sampled at up to 2 MHz, smoothed with a 100-sample (50 µs) moving average; window alignment not stated
input_target_timing.outputs: TS Te and ne profiles (TS repetition rate up to 120 Hz)
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: TS reported profiles serve as labels. The authors suggest the network suppresses TS outliers (Fig.11, PDF p.12); this is their interpretation, not independent truth.

validation.unknowns: chronological split, centered vs trailing smoothing, test set beyond validation folds, confidence intervals

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Authors state inference of about 0.1 ms per profile; the measurement conditions are not described
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Real-time deployment, latency budget, and accuracy between TS times (sawtooth/ELM traces in Fig.18-19 are qualitative)

forbidden_inferences: that the method is causal or noncausal
validated microsecond accuracy between TS samples
that it applies to CES or ion temperature
that its sensitivity maps identify physical mechanisms
that its 0.1 ms figure relates to our 10 ms grid
priority claims relative to our work
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. It maps an instantaneous fast-diagnostic snapshot to slow labels without anchoring on past reports. Our framing (strictly past CES reports plus BES/ECEI voltages, compared against hold, causal GP and two-sided interpolation) addresses a different timing question. It should not be framed as a deficiency of this paper.
